info.description: The admin API the panel calls, with an administrator's session. It is served on its own listener, meant to be reachable only from where administrators work.
info.name: Loginer Admin API

item.description: Get admin-cli's token first: it is stored in {{admin_token}}, which the other requests send.

request.description: Client credentials for admin-cli, for the admin API. The token's scopes are the permissions admin-cli is allowed in the panel.

item.name: Start here

item.description: Whether the server is up, for load balancers and uptime checks.

request.description: Says the server is up.

item.name: Health

item.description: Creating the first administrator of a new installation.

request.description: Says whether the panel still needs its first administrator.
Makes the first administrator: a super admin, with the address and password whoever is setting the panel up chose.

item.name: First administrator

item.description: Signing an administrator in and out, and who is signed in.

request.description: Checks the credentials and sets the session cookie.

Reports how far this browser's session has got (password, code, enrolment).

It needs no session.
Finishes a sign-in waiting for a second factor.
Revokes the session and clears the cookie.

Returns the signed-in administrator, and tells the browser whether its session is still alive.

The organisation's public name and logo come with it for the panel's header.
Changes the caller's own name and address, nothing else, so every administrator may use it.

Sets the caller's own password, given the one they have.

Every other session they have open ends; the one they are using stays.
Lists the caller's own sessions, so they can see where they are signed in.

Signs one of the administrator's other browsers out.

Another administrator's session is answered as not found.
Signs the administrator out everywhere but here: what to do after using a shared computer, or losing a laptop.

item.name: Signing in

item.description: An administrator's authenticator app and recovery codes.

request.description: Describes the administrator's second factor.
Starts setting up an authenticator app, and answers the secret and the otpauth URI to show as a QR code.
Finishes setting up with a code from the app, and answers the recovery codes — the only time they are shown.
Turns two-factor sign-in off.
Replaces the recovery codes.

item.name: Second factor

item.description: The server's own OpenAPI document, for your tooling.

request.description: Answers the OpenAPI document.

item.name: OpenAPI document

item.description: The dashboard's counts and the activity log.

request.description:
Is the panel's front page for a range of days: totals, sign-in outcomes, daily activity, the busiest people and the latest entries.

Its five reads run concurrently.
Lists one page of the activity log, newest first, narrowed by the filters parseFilter reads, with the cursor the next page starts from.
Writes matching entries as CSV, newest first, up to exportLimit, hiding exactly what the logs page hides.

item.name: Activity

item.description: The people your organisation manages.

request.description: Returns a page of users, newest first. `search` matches the email and any field text.
Returns one user.

Returns the roles a user holds as a token would carry them: global roles and each application's, direct and inherited. `client_id` narrows to one application; applications the administrator cannot see are left out.

Returns every role a user holds, direct and inherited, with what each comes through.

Roles of invisible applications are left out.
Adds a user.
Replaces a user's email, verified flag and fields, and the password too when a new one is given.
Removes a user for good.
Removes a provider a user signs in with; their account and other ways in remain.

Gives a user roles directly, keeping existing ones.

Each needs role_assignments.write for its scope; one refusal refuses the request.
Removes a directly held role; an inherited one is removed by removing what it comes through.

item.name: Users

item.description: The custom fields a user record is made of.

request.description:
Returns the fields a user record has, in the order they are shown.

The panel builds both its table and its form from this.

Adds a field to every user record.

Existing users simply have no value for it until they are edited.

Changes a field's rules.

Name and type never change, since records hold values under them.
Removes a field; stored values are dropped when each user is next saved.

item.name: User fields

item.description: Who is signed in, and signing them out.

request.description: Returns a page of active sessions, newest first.
Ends every session a user has and revokes every refresh token their applications hold, so they are signed out everywhere at once.

Signs one session out.

The user's applications keep their tokens: it is the browser that is signed out, as when the user ends it themselves.

item.name: User sessions

item.description: The organisation's name, branding and agreements.

request.description: Returns the organisation.

Changes the settings.

What a request leaves out is left as it is, so a client that knows about one field does not clear the rest.

item.name: Organization

item.description: Signing in with an account at another provider.

request.description: Returns every configured provider, and the kinds a new one may be.
Returns one provider.

Returns the stored client secret so it can be checked against the provider's console.

It requires the permission that could replace it, and every read is written to the activity log.

Registers a provider.

Its credentials are proved only by a first sign-in.

Changes a provider's settings.

Kind and slug are fixed, since they form the registered callback address.
Removes a provider and its identities; the accounts stay, though some may lose their only way in.

item.name: Social providers

item.description: Signing in through a customer's own identity provider, over OpenID Connect or SAML.

request.description: Returns every connection, with how many people sign in through each.
Returns one connection.

Adds a connection, disabled until an administrator turns it on.

A SAML connection gets its own signing key and certificate.
Tries a provider before it is relied on: an OpenID Connect issuer's discovery, or a SAML provider's metadata, from its address or as pasted.

Changes a connection.

Its slug and protocol are not among them: both are in the addresses its provider was given.

Removes a connection and the identities held at it.

The accounts stay, and sign in however else they can.
Reads a SAML provider's metadata again from its address — for when it has rolled its certificate over.

item.name: Single sign-on

item.description: The steps a sign-in goes through, per application.

request.description: Returns every flow, the steps one can be made of, and how many applications each flow signs people in for.
Returns one flow.
Adds a flow, disabled until an administrator enables it.

Changes a flow.

Its identifier is not among them: an application and an export both name a flow by it.

Removes a flow.

The applications signing people in with it fall back to the default, which is why the default itself cannot go.

item.name: Login flows

item.description: The sign-in pages' languages and their text.

request.description: Returns every language, with how much of each app it translates, and the shipped languages this installation does not have.
Returns one language's text for one app, for the editor.
Adds a language, with the text it starts from (createRequest).
Changes a language's names and whether and where it is offered.

Removes a language and its text.

Anybody who had chosen it is shown the default from their next page on.

Replaces one language's text for one app.

Unknown keys are dropped and counted, so older files still import.

item.name: Languages

item.description: The applications that sign users in: their settings, secrets and API access.

request.description: Returns a page of the applications the administrator can see, sorted by name, each with how many roles it defines.
Returns one application.

Replaces an application's settings.

Its type and client id stay as they are: every copy of the app already in use depends on both.

Replaces a confidential client's secret.

The old one stops working at once, so the app has to be given the new one straight away.
Lists every API with what the application may do with it: whether it is authorised to ask for tokens for it, and which scopes.
Lets the application request tokens for an API and replaces the scopes it may ask for: the ceiling on its tokens.
Stops the application asking for tokens for an API.
Runs the token endpoint's evaluation without issuing anything: whether a token is issued, each scope decision, and the claims.

Registers an application.

A confidential client is given its secret here, in the answer, and never again: only its hash is kept.

Removes an application, the roles it defines, and everyone's hold on them.

Tokens it has already issued stay valid until they expire.

item.name: Applications

item.description: The roles users hold, globally and in each application.

request.description: Returns a page of roles sorted by name, each with its member count and every role it includes. `scope` is "global", "application" or empty for both; `application` narrows to one application.

query.description: Space-separated scopes: `openid`, `profile`, `email`, `offline_access`, `roles`, and the scopes of the API named in `audience`.

request.description: Returns one role.
Adds a role: a global one when application_id is null, otherwise one of that application's.

Replaces a role's name, description, default flag and inheritance.

Its scope never changes.

Removes a role for good.

The users who held it keep everything else they hold, and the roles that included it simply stop.

item.name: User roles

item.description: The APIs access tokens are issued for, and their scopes.

request.description: Returns every API matching the search, sorted by name, with its scopes and how many applications may use it.
Returns one API.

Lists visible applications with their access to the API.

Access is changed through the application's endpoints.
Lists changes to the API and applications gaining or losing access, newest first.
Registers an API with its scopes.

Replaces an API's name, description, role enforcement and scopes.

The identifier never changes.

Removes an API with its scopes, application authorisations and role grants.

Issued tokens stay valid until they expire.

item.name: APIs

item.description: The panel's administrators.

request.description: Returns the administrators' sign-in settings and how many have an authenticator.

Changes those settings.

Requiring a second factor applies on each administrator's next page load.
Returns a page of administrators, newest first.
Adds an administrator, with the password and roles the super admin chose for them.
Returns one administrator.

Replaces an administrator's details, status, roles and optionally password.

A new password, or losing the right to sign in, ends their sessions.

Removes an administrator for good.

Nobody can remove themselves: that is how a panel ends up with no one able to manage it.

Removes another administrator's second factor and signs them out everywhere.

Your own is managed from your profile with a code.

item.name: Administrators

item.description: How email is sent, and what each message says.

request.description: Returns the mail settings.
Changes the settings; omitted fields stay, including the password unless a new one is typed.

Sends one message with the form's settings, so a server can be tried before saving.

Without a typed password the stored one is used.
Returns every email's text in each offered language, with English beside it.

Writes one language's email text, merging only the email keys.

Any other key is refused as a client bug.

item.name: Mail

item.description: How the one-time codes sent by email behave.

request.description: Returns the settings and the login flows that use emailed codes.

Changes the settings.

What a request leaves out is left as it is.

item.name: One-time codes

item.description: The keys tokens are signed with, and rotating them.

request.description: Describes every published key: the one signing, the next one waiting, and the retired ones still published.
Makes new keys now.

item.name: Signing keys

item.description: What the Redis cache holds, and clearing it.

request.description: Sums up both databases: how many keys of each kind, each group's generation and what it holds, and the Redis server they share.
Lists a page of one database's keys.
Answers one key and what it holds.

Replaces a cached value by hand.

Only a value of a group's current generation in the cache database can be: see cache.Write.

Removes one key.

The next request that wanted it reads the database again.
Forgets everything cached in one group, for every server process at once.

Removes every key this server keeps in one database.

Flushing sessions signs nobody out, but resets every rate limit.

item.name: Cache

item.description: What administrators may do in the panel.

request.description: Returns the catalog roles pick from, in the order the panel lists it.
Returns every admin role matching the search, sorted by name, with how many administrators hold each.
Adds an admin role.

Replaces an admin role's name, description and permissions.

Every administrator holding it has the new permissions on their next request.

Removes an admin role.

The administrators who held it keep their other roles.

item.name: Administrator roles

variable.description: The public server's address, where tokens come from.
The panel's address, where the admin API is reached.
admin-cli's secret: rotate it in the panel and paste it here.
Filled in by "Get an admin-cli token".
An administrator's session cookie, for the routes only a person may call.
